Shared adapter library: catalogue search and size filter, Hugging Face files checked before download
items.body:
The adapter library now matches ACE-Step Studio's, the shared version in
music-studio-core:
- Hugging Face results show downloads beside likes, and can also search
  repository names (the catalogue's hub.search words).
- A repository's files are checked by their safetensors header before
  download: the format (LoRA, LoKr) and why the engine cannot merge a file
  (LoHa, DoRA), read in music-core's adapter_weights.
- The catalogue can be searched and, for a model that comes in several sizes,
  filtered by size; an adapter of the other size is marked.
- music_engine::model is where a model plugs in: its adapter slots, its sizes,
  and what an adapter file is for its engine.

items.body:
A wait answers within 55 s, under the minute clients give a tool call, and
says to call again. Every answer that is a library song leaves out its
audio codes, score, duplicated lyrics and karaoke timings unless asked for
detailed; the recogniser settings list the models to choose, not every
file. The page reading gives one line per song row with its buttons. A
cover names the library song its melody came from (cover_of, from the
cover page or an agent), video_get reports the clip's length once the audio
is loaded, the tool list is fresh for five minutes, and the skill says the
video editor needs a visible window.

items.subject: MCP: short answers an agent acts on, models_adopt, song_defaults, plain paths
items.body:
A song job answers with its status and the songs it made instead of the
request's lyrics, score and audio codes; a library song leaves its audio
codes out; lora_list gives one line per LoRA in English; studio_wait and
studio_status speak of jobs the same way. response_format detailed gives
everything. A just-installed LoRA says its slots are not known yet instead
of an empty list. Adopting model files takes a folder path, so an agent
can do it without the folder dialog, and song_defaults tells what a field
left out becomes. File paths come without the \\?\ prefix, and cover_prompt
says it needs an image model set up.

items.subject: MCP on the 2026-07-28 revision; the agent as the studio's assistant; tracks made by tools are tracks of the library
items.body:
The server speaks the stateless revision (server/discover, per-request
_meta, Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name checked against the body, cacheable lists,
structured results, portable schemas) and the handshake revisions for
older clients. Picking "Agent (MCP)" as the writing assistant sends what
the studio would ask its local model to the connected agent; Settings has
an Agent page with the connection state and what to paste. The agent reads
and fills the create page's form, sees each control with its label and
the song it belongs to, plays a single stem, shows the user a message and
reads the window's console. Every song_create field is in its schema.

items.subject: MCP: local origins only, one window per command, streamed uploads
items.body:
The MCP endpoint and the window bridge refuse a foreign Origin, so a web
page cannot make the studio read files by path. A command goes to the
newest window only, not to every open one. Tools that install, import or
refresh are no longer annotated read-only. Files an agent names are sent
to the route a megabyte at a time instead of whole in memory, and a clip
of a long song fits the videos route. A failed render reports its reason
in video_get instead of an alert, and writer: agent refuses to train
before the agent has written the songs.

items.subject: Site: the agent over MCP
An MCP server in the studio
items.body:
Every route of the studio's API is a tool called inside the process, named
by area (song_, library_, dataset_, training_, lora_...), annotated, with
large answers cut to what an agent acts on and studio_wait instead of
polling. The window answers through a bridge: a screenshot, its controls,
clicks and typing, the pages, the player and the video editor, whose clip
an agent's render saves in the studio's folder. MiniMax's caption rules and
reference captions are tools, resources and prompts, and a preparation can
leave the lyric layout to the agent (writer: agent).

Stop choices short enough to fit their field

The folders a song came from name its artist when its tags do not; the
source kept only the file name, so that was lost once the upload was done.

A caption written by the assistant marks the song's style done
items.body:
The describe route stored the caption but left the song's style state
wanted, so the song still showed as lacking a style.

items.subject: Guide timings measured; repeated lines marked for the section model
items.body:
The guide gives what MOSS was measured to take on an RTX 4090 (about 12 GB,
6-7 s a song). The numbered sheet the assistant sections marks each line
sung more than once with its count, so a small model sees the chorus.

items.subject: Project pages: dataset preparation and describing by ear
items.body:
A card for the one-drop dataset preparation, a requirements row for
MOSS-Music, and no song-count limit on the own-LoRA card, in every language.

items.subject: Second review pass on dataset preparation
items.body:
A batch Whisper run the card refuses goes on on the processor with only the
songs still unheard, and the page says so. A title starting with a number
keeps it unless the number is a zero-padded or three-digit track number.
Lyrics lookup compiles its patterns once, and a short title no longer
matches a longer one that merely contains it.

items.subject: Review fixes for the preparation job
items.body:
A song deleted mid-job fails alone instead of stopping the job; the job
file is written before the job is marked running; a listen callback no
longer waits forever when the tempo measurer dies; an unreadable dataset
is reported instead of leaving a stale queue. Triggers made from names in
other scripts carry a hash, and a trigger the user cleared stays cleared.
The dataset card and the train step count readiness by song state.

items.subject: Dataset preparation as a resumable server job
items.body:
Lyrics come from LRCLIB, QQ Music and Kugou first; only songs none of them
knows are separated and heard by Whisper, with hallucinations filtered. Each
song keeps its lyrics and style state in dataset.json, the job is kept on
disk and picked up after a restart, and a failed song can be finished alone.
A published sheet is laid out by section boundaries, so its words stay exact;
the assistant schema is sent where llama-server reads it. MOSS listens with
the tempo (and in MiniMax the key) measured on the card, models load one at a
time and once per batch, and the engine watcher leaves a busy card alone.
The wizard shows every stage live; datasets get a trigger word from their
name; README lists every model with its link and folder.

items.subject: Training guide: a window that stays over the page, dragged and resized, with the workflow, what to write, what the studio does and does not do, the run settings and a checklist
Auto skips Vulkan beside an NVIDIA card; an engine that dies without a word counts as a lost device
items.body:
The DiT on Vulkan hung an RTX 4090 until Windows reset its driver (three
nvlddmkm resets, with and without flash attention), and the engine left
nothing in its log, so the chain would have restarted it on Vulkan again.
Auto now goes CUDA then the processor on NVIDIA, and a silent death under
Auto moves down the chain. The Vulkan hint says NVIDIA should use CUDA.

items.subject: Engine at minimaxmusic.cpp 8e6d54f: the device is chosen and tested before the engine listens
Auto walks CUDA, Vulkan, the processor: a device that fails is left for the session
items.body:
The engine now tests the device it chose before it takes work. Under
Auto the studio starts it on CUDA, then Vulkan, then the processor,
moving on when a start fails or the engine dies with a CUDA or Vulkan
error, never on running out of memory. A device chosen in Settings is
the only one tried. Engine at minimaxmusic.cpp 8b36200.

items.subject: Vulkan and a compute device setting: Auto, CUDA, Vulkan or the processor
items.body:
The engine is built with Vulkan beside the two CUDA backends, so AMD and
Intel cards and NVIDIA cards neither CUDA build runs have a GPU path.
Off CUDA the engine's FP16 clamp is on, as in YuE2 Studio.

items.subject: 1.6.2: every NVIDIA card from the GTX 900 series, two CUDA builds with device code; engine at minimaxmusic.cpp 120a4f6
Ship cudart64_12.dll beside the engine for the CUDA 12 backend
Build the CUDA 12 backend with the MSVC 14.4x toolset nvcc 12.9 knows
Run on every NVIDIA card from the GTX 900 series: two CUDA builds, device code only
items.body:
The engine now loads its backends at run time and ships a CUDA 13 and a
CUDA 12.9 ggml-cuda, each in its own folder; the studio reads the
compute capability and the driver from nvidia-smi and names the one
they run, fetching that build's cuBLAS. Every architecture gets device
code, so an older driver no longer fails on PTX it cannot compile.
Cards before Ampere get the engine's FP16 clamp.

and the portable build. 8a5e42c4 keeps a chain entry with no saved state

items.subject: Processing: a chain of the user's own VST3 plugins, before mastering
items.body:
HOT-Step's vst-host runs beside the studio as its own process, so a plugin
that crashes takes the host down and not the studio. It finds the plugins in
the system's VST3 folders, opens a plugin's own window to set it up - the
settings saved into a state file per chain slot - and runs a track through
the enabled plugins at its own rate. The processing window gains the chain;
a kept version's name lists the plugins.

items.subject: Training exports HOT-PiZZA as plain LoRA; the window fits a 24 GB card with room
items.body:
The recipe asks the trainer (43fd0732) for standalone PiSSA exports - a
plain rank-2r LoRA the engine merges - where the default wrote deltas tied
to a residual file, and holds the frozen factors in F16. The first run on a
24 GB card left 0.5 GB free at a 2048 frame window; the default is now 1536.

items.subject: Tools page: the processing window opens on the track chosen there
Datasets import from other studios; captions written by the assistant
items.body:
A dataset folder from YuE2 Studio imports as it stands, and a dataset's
folder opens to be carried the other way. Each song's structured caption -
Global Metadata, Vocal Details, Arrangement - can be written by the writing
assistant from its style line and lyrics, retried once when a section comes
back empty; the answer is capped at 2048 tokens (a transcript at 4096) so a
looping model fails fast. Uploads to a dataset may weigh up to 16 GB. The
engine moves to minimaxmusic.cpp 7fca80a, which honours rsLoRA.

items.subject: LoRA page and training on MiniMax Music 3
items.body:
The LoRA page comes over from YuE2 Studio: installed adapters, the catalogue,
Hugging Face search and imports, and a picker in the create form that puts a
LoRA's trigger word into the Global Metadata and brings a song's LoRA back
when it is reused. Song details show the parameters this engine records.

items.subject: LoRA on the server: the engine loads the studio's adapters into the LM and the DiT
items.body:
The engine moves to the timoncool/minimaxmusic.cpp fork, which merges LoRA
and LoKr adapters into the planner LM and the flow DiT at load and shifts a
short schedule to keep its sound. The studio starts it with its adapter
folder, and a request names installed adapters with a strength for the
composition (the LM) and the sound (the DiT).

items.subject: Audio processing, and MP3 made by the studio with LAME
items.body:
Processing comes over from YuE2 Studio as it now stands: noise reduction,
Spectral Lifter, the vocal naturalizer and mastering to a reference, run into
a preview that is kept as a version beside the original or thrown away. Runs
are claimed atomically and clean up after themselves.

README: correct the portable models path
items.body:
Portable builds keep their data beside the executable in a data\ folder, so
the models live in <unzipped>\data\models\minimaxmusic-cpp\, not
<unzipped>\models\minimaxmusic-cpp\ as the model-zoo note claimed. Reported in
issue #2; confirmed against desktop\src-tauri\src\lib.rs where the portable
data root is executable_directory().join("data").

items.subject: chore: update star history chart
Document the model zoo and the engine's DLLs; fix the site's VRAM tiers
items.body:
README gains a full model zoo - every GGUF with a direct download link, its
size, the profile that uses it and where the two source repositories publish
it - plus the folder they belong in, so a file placed by hand is recognised as
installed. A new section explains the engine's DLL chain: what ships inside the
app, that cuBLAS comes from NVIDIA's own redistributable and the VC++ runtime
from Microsoft, what is never downloaded (the driver's nvcuda.dll), and how to
place the libraries by hand behind a proxy or offline. The release note now
reflects that the script reads the signing key from %USERPROFILE%\.tauri.

items.subject: Fix three user reports, and take the audio-input feature back out
items.body:
Audio in is gone from the build - card, endpoints, encoder, request field,
strings. The engine only replays codes whole: the output was always the same
music read back a little muddier, and the caption could not change it. It was a
debug tool dressed as a feature. The ONNX-runtime path helper it left behind
stays; the separator uses it.

items.subject: Read a finished track and render it again
items.body:
The encoder MiniMax never published was rebuilt by the community and exported
to ONNX months ago; it sat in the repository unused, called from nowhere. It is
wired up now: a track is dropped on the card or chosen, it plays there with its
waveform, and the studio reads it into the codes the engine renders from. The
next generation replays them - the melody and the structure come from the file,
the sound from the caption and the lyrics, which still build the prompt the
codes are replayed through. Nothing changes for a request without a track.

items.subject: Ask each model for thinking on the terms it publishes
items.body:
OpenRouter describes every model's reasoning in a field of its own - not inside
default_parameters, which is where this was looking. The record says which
efforts the model takes, which one it prefers, and whether it can be asked not
to think at all:

items.subject: Write down what the cloud was asked, and let a run be given up on
items.body:
A request that went wrong left one red line and nothing behind it: the answer
was gone the moment the window closed, and a model that wrote almost the right
thing looked exactly like one that wrote nothing. Every call to OpenRouter is
now recorded beside the engine's log - what was asked, how long it took, what
came back, and the answer itself whenever it could not be used. The key is
never written. Read it at /v1/openrouter/logs or open the file.

items.subject: Open the assistant on the engine that was chosen
items.body:
Switching the assistant to OpenRouter worked and then came back to llama.cpp on
every open. The panel draws itself from one address - the runtime - and the
chosen engine is kept with the assistant's settings, which that address never
mentioned. So it fell back to the first tab, every time, whatever had been
saved.

items.subject: Say what the karaoke switch does, and write the news
items.body:
The switch reads "enable karaoke", which sounds like permission. It is not:
with it on, every finished track is timed automatically - that is the whole of
what it does - so it now says so in all five languages.

items.subject: Leave the tab where the user left it
items.body:
Pressing "write the lyrics and the description" filled the form and then moved
the screen to the Studio tab, on the grounds that this is where the writing
becomes visible. It is also where the user was not: they had chosen the simple
tab and were working there. Looking at what was written is their decision to
make, one click away.

items.subject: Let the karaoke button work once the recogniser is installed
items.body:
A complete installation still answered "karaoke.model-missing": a faster-whisper
model is a directory of files, and the readiness check asked whether that path
was a file. It never is. The download finished, the panel said ready, and the
button refused.

items.subject: Recognise lyrics with faster-whisper, the way Dub Studio does
items.body:
Karaoke timings failed with "whisper-cli produced no LRC file" and that is all
anyone could learn: whisper.cpp writes its LRC line by line, word times had to
be inferred from it, and when a run went wrong the binary exited zero and wrote
nothing at all.

items.subject: Clear the batch ceiling out of the engine settings entirely
Take the batch slider out of the interface
Put the batch ceiling back to one and take its control away
items.body:
The variations slider was unlocked to four, and to make it work the engine had
to be started with --max-batch 4. That flag reserves the language model's KV
cache for the whole batch when the weights load, so every single-song
generation - which is nearly all of them - would have paid for three songs it
never rendered. Worse, the engine takes it only as a launch flag: there is no
way to raise it for one request and lower it after, so no amount of interface
makes it a live control.

items.subject: Tell the engine the batch ceiling, and keep its log across a crash
items.body:
Asking for two songs failed at once with a 503. The panel offers up to four and
the request carries the number, which is what was checked - but the engine has
a ceiling of its own, set by --max-batch when the weights load, because it
sizes the language model's KV sets. The studio never passed it, so the engine
loaded with the upstream default of one and refused anything above it. It is
passed now, and a test holds the two together: what the panel offers is what
the engine is started with.

items.subject: Make every panel a whole capability
items.body:
Downloading Gemma left the studio insisting no assistant was set up. The panel
showed a model chosen and installed; the server had no record of which one,
because the dropdown saved its choice for Whisper only and installing did not
record it either - and readiness is decided by exactly that field. Choosing a
model is now a setting for the assistant and for Parakeet's two precisions as
well, and asking for a download records the model it fetches.

items.subject: Let a download be stopped
items.body:
Two downloads could be started by accident and neither could be stopped: the
only way out was to quit the studio. Each panel now has a stop button beside
its percentage, and each capability an endpoint behind it.

items.subject: Back off exponentially, the way the Hub's download protocol asks
Follow the Hub's rate limit instead of walking into it
items.body:
The download died with "429 Too Many Requests where 206 was expected", and the
flood was ours. Asking the servers what a file weighs marked a URL as known
only when the answer arrived, and the panel polls its status every second: two
dozen HEAD requests per second for as long as a page was open. The Hub allows
three thousand requests per five minute window, so that emptied it in about a
minute - and then refused the download the user was actually waiting for.

items.subject: Fetch every model over four connections, and stop trusting compiled-in sizes
items.body:
Three of the assistant's models could never install. Their sizes were written
into the catalogue when they were added, unsloth re-uploaded the files, and the
download check - "the file must weigh exactly this" - failed on 1440 bytes of
changed metadata for ever. What a file weighs is the server's answer, not ours,
so it is asked for and no longer assumed.

items.subject: Let a request ask for up to four songs at once
One place installs a capability, and it reports the set it installs
items.body:
A capability could be installed from three screens - the providers page, its
own settings page and the download panel - each with its own buttons, its own
list of files and its own idea of progress. They disagreed: the same assistant
read "0/8" in one place and "not installed" in another. The settings pages now
use the download panel's group, and the providers page only chooses where a
capability runs.

items.subject: Read audio, not only write it
items.body:
MiniMax published Music 3 without the encoder that turns audio into the codes
the model generates, so a finished track could never be handed back to it. The
community reconstructed the weights; this exports them to ONNX, publishes the
result, and wires the path through parts the studio already has - neural-codec
for audio to latents, ONNX Runtime for latents to codes, and the engine's own
audio_codes field to render from them. The export is verified against the
PyTorch reference with every code identical.

items.subject: An instrumental keeps a song's structure instead of alternating [instrumental]
Say that the budget counter counts the caption as well
Make every optional engine the same choice, stated the same way
items.body:
Karaoke, stems and the assistant each asked the user something different: a
list of file names, a device toggle in another panel, or nothing at all. They
are now one shape - which engine, what it runs on, which model - in one row
that says what it weighs and whether it is here, with download and remove
beside it.

items.subject: An instrumental submits no lyrics, whatever is left in the box
One button per engine, and a device choice for the assistant too
Supervise the engine, and make every local engine a choice
items.body:
The engine was started once at launch and only with weights already on disk,
so a clean install downloaded its models and then waited forever - the state
every new user ended in. A supervisor now watches the engine port and starts
it whenever a complete set is present, which also covers a crash.

items.subject: Drop the MSI: it installed per-machine and put the models on the system drive
Ship only the per-user installer, which can keep its data beside itself
Keep an installed studio's data beside itself, and wait for the libraries it needs
Read the binary name from the config the portable build copies
Give the installed and portable executables the same name
Keep the signing password beside the key the release script reads
Fail the release on an unusable signing key, and stop building what is not shipped
items.body:
An encrypted signing key with no password does not fail the build - Tauri
asks for it on stdin, the build has no console, and the release sits in
silence with the installers already written. The key is now read before
anything is built, and an encrypted one without a password is refused with
its reason.

items.subject: Keep the generated release config out of the repository
Stop holding the graphics card when nothing is using it
items.body:
The writing assistant kept its five gigabytes after answering, so Music3
asked for eleven more on a 24 GB card and died - and the studio showed a
queued job that would never run. The assistant is unloaded as soon as it
answers and again before the engine starts, unless "keep models in VRAM
between jobs" is on. It starts itself on the next request, so the only cost
is a reload.

items.subject: Let a refused optional download reach the button that asked for it
items.body:
The separation endpoint started the download inside a spawned task and
discarded its Result, then answered "started: true" whatever happened. The
downloader takes one job at a time, so a second request came back refused -
into a void - while the caller was told it had begun. Pressing the button
did nothing, twice, with a successful reply behind it.

items.subject: Install the libraries the engine cannot start without
items.body:
mm-server.exe loads ggml.dll, which loads ggml-cuda.dll, which imports
cublas64_13.dll and through it cublasLt64_13.dll - static imports, resolved
by the Windows loader before any of the engine's own code runs. Neither was
shipped, so on a machine without the CUDA Toolkit the process died in the
loader and no fallback to the processor was possible. The build machine had
them on PATH, which is why this survived a release.

items.subject: build: the manifest points at the installer of the version being built
docs: 1.3.1 in the version, the changelog and the news
fix: the studio downloads, deletes and runs what was actually chosen
items.body: Every one of these was found by using the thing, not by reading it.

items.subject: feat: a local model downloads itself the first time it is used
items.body:
Choosing Parakeet or Whisper in the settings is the instruction to use it.
Making the user then hunt for a download button is a second instruction nobody
gave, so the first track that needs timings fetches the model and carries on -
from the automatic pass and from the button in the track menu alike.

items.subject: feat: a portable copy keeps everything inside its own folder
items.body:
People found ten gigabytes of weights in their profile directory and no way to
remove them from inside the studio. Both halves are fixed.

items.subject: docs: each language page actually shows its language
items.body:
The generator read docs/index.html, which after the first run was itself a
generated English page carrying apply('en'). Every later run copied that into
all five files, so ru.html, zh.html, ja.html and ko.html rendered English while
claiming their own lang attribute.

items.subject: docs: a donate page in every language the studio speaks
docs: the support button goes where money is taken, not to a file in the repository
docs: one page per language, and the agent config stops being published
docs: follow the branch rename to main
docs: point the donate and history links at the branch that exists
docs: keep local engineering notes out of the published repository
build: the release script says where its signing key lives
docs: record where the signing key lives and what 1.3.0 shipped
build: make the release script survive its own toolchain
items.body:
Four things stood between this repository and a signed release, each fatal only
at the end of a long build. PowerShell 5.1 turns a native program's stderr into
a terminating error when output is redirected, so cargo's warnings and git's
"Cloning into" killed the run; exit codes decide now. A function returning the
compiler's output as its value poisoned the staged runtime path. Windows
refused the engine checkout path once the full commit hash was in it. And the
updater manifest was written with an encoding that only exists in PowerShell 7.

items.subject: docs: reshoot the studio in five languages and say what it does now
items.body:
The screenshots on the page and in the readme were taken before the M3 icon,
the model presets, the rebuilt tools panel and stem separation existed, and
three of the five languages were missing half the screens.

items.subject: docs: name the replay for what it does
items.body:
"Rebuild the track" read as "generate it again". It re-renders the same
melody from the saved audio codes; only steps, seed, DiT CFG and the
output format can differ. The label says so now, in every language.

items.subject: feat: stems on the graphics card, a transport that seeks, a cover you can see
items.body:
- The separator can run on the card: the CUDA build of the ONNX Runtime
  is a listed optional download, the setting is auto / card / processor,
  and auto takes the card whenever its runtime is present. Registering
  the provider is attempted and falls back to the processor out loud
  rather than silently taking ten times as long.
- Stems are served with byte ranges. Without them a player cannot seek at
  all, which is why dragging their position did nothing.
- Stems play through the studio's own transport instead of the browser's
  default widget: click or drag the bar to move, arrows for five seconds.
- The cover window shows the result at 360 pixels square, and a click
  opens it full screen with wheel zoom, drag to pan, double-click to fit.
- The menu entry is "Split into stems" and opens the track on the tools
  page, where the choices and the results are. "Video export" is "Create
  video". The profile line under the create form opens the page that
  changes it, instead of stating a fact the user cannot act on.
- Downloads carry ID3: a track made before tagging existed is tagged on
  its way out, so an old file no longer arrives untitled.

items.subject: feat: separation where it belongs, and an editor that opens
items.body:
- The model is listed with the other optional modules on the models page,
  beside the assistant and karaoke, and downloads from there.
- Which stems to keep and how carefully to join the segments are chosen
  on the tools page, next to the button that uses them, and both are
  remembered. Verified: asking for two stems at the fastest overlap wrote
  exactly those two.
- The track is picked by search from a bounded list. A native dropdown
  showed whole generated captions as options and grew to any width; a
  library of five thousand tracks is not a list to scroll.
- "Stems" is in the track menu everywhere the menu appears: library,
  song list, player and the sidebar.
- The waveform editor is served by the studio itself and opened in the
  system browser. It was opened with window.open on a relative path,
  which does nothing at all inside the desktop shell.

items.subject: feat: the tools page is about tools now
items.body:
It was a diagnostics screen with nothing to do on it. The diagnostics
belong next to the flags that produce them, so the engine log moved into
Settings → Local engine, and this page became what its name says: work
done to a finished track.

items.subject: fix: the desktop crate needs serde_json now that the configuration carries plugins
items.body:
`tauri::generate_context!` expands to code that names serde_json as soon
as tauri.conf.json has a plugin section, and the updater is one.

items.subject: feat: stems, separated natively instead of in a browser tab
items.body:
ACE-Step Studio split tracks with an ONNX build of htdemucs running under
WebAssembly on a page of its own. That is the arrangement this studio
replaced everywhere else; here it is replaced too.

items.subject: chore: the star chart is rendered here, not fetched from a broken service
items.body:
GitHub closed the public stargazers endpoint, so star-history.com and
starchart.cc cannot draw this repository's chart. The Action that renders
it from the repository's own token is back, with the first SVG already
committed so the README is not blank until Monday.

items.subject: chore: merge master; the star chart is a live badge now, not a checked-in SVG
feat: ID3 tags, covers that fit, a settings home for cover looks
items.body:
- MP3s the studio stores now carry ID3v2.4: title, artist, album, genre
  when the description states one, TBPM, the lyrics and the cover art.
  Verified on a real track: TIT2/TALB/TPE1/TBPM/USLT and a 6 MB APIC read
  back off disk. Section labels never become a genre, and a structured
  caption with no genre in it leaves the field empty rather than filing
  every track under "Global Metadata".
- Saving a generated cover failed with "Failed to fetch": axum's default
  body limit is two megabytes and a cover is more. Raised to 256 MB, and
  an 8 MB payload now stores.
- Cover looks are a settings page of their own: templates, placeholders,
  a live example of what the prompt becomes, and the one new covers start
  from. The cover window opens on that default and has room to write in.
- External links did nothing in the packaged application because the
  dialogs stop click propagation, so the document-level handler never
  saw them. It listens in the capture phase now.
- Titles follow ACE-Step Studio's own rule, read out of its source rather
  than guessed: the chorus line, then any sung line, then the description.
- The changelog starts at this project's first commit; it was showing
  ACE-Step's entire history.

items.subject: docs: record what was verified in this round
docs: a project page in five languages, screenshots from the running studio
items.body:
The repository looked like a source tree and not like something anyone
could decide to install:

items.subject: feat: local reasoning flags, a set you can switch, names for unnamed tracks
items.body:
- llama-server is started with --reasoning/--reasoning-budget and
  --reasoning-format deepseek, driven by the same setting the cloud path
  sends as reasoning.effort, instead of leaving thinking to chance.
- /setup/select uses a set that is already on disk, so a machine with two
  quantisations installed is no longer stuck on whichever downloaded last.
- Settings shows the resource page, not the first-run page: no "first run"
  badge, no hardware recommendation banner, and a "use this set" button.
- A request with no title is named the way ACE-Step Studio names one: the
  first sung line, or the first words of the style.
- The provider panel shows the model the studio would use, so a key alone
  is enough to start.
- Cover prompts are templates with {title}/{style}/{excerpt}/{duration},
  saved between runs and filled in from the track the cover is for.
- A window whose service has died says so instead of counting seconds at
  an engine that is not starting.
- opener:allow-open-url carries a scope; without one the plugin refused
  every external link in the packaged application.

items.subject: fix: each model's own sampling, a catalog that is fetched once, and links that open
items.body: Three things that were the program's job, not the user's.

items.subject: fix: the download page only when something is missing, and a catalog worth choosing from
items.body:
The studio showed its first-run page on every launch, for the second before it
knew anything, and again while the engine was starting - so a fully installed
machine was repeatedly shown a 26 GB bill. There are three states now, and the
unknown one is a wait rather than a decision: the download page appears only
once the studio has answered that components are genuinely missing.

items.subject: feat: the engine's own screen, real news, a changelog from git, and links that open
items.body:
The first run and the engine starting were the same page, so a fully
installed studio was shown a 26 GB download while it waited three seconds for
a process. They are separate now: the download page appears only when
components are missing, the engine gets its own quiet screen with the step it
is on, a moving bar, the seconds, and its log; and choosing quantisations
afterwards lives in Settings → Models, where a settings decision belongs.

items.subject: fix: no orphans, no waiting for a button, and a first run that shows its work
items.body: Three things a user should never have to do for the program.

items.subject: fix: fetch the OpenRouter catalog when it is needed, and say the assistant is working
items.body:
Pressing the assistant button answered "Refresh the OpenRouter catalog before
using the assistant" - pointing at a button on another screen, for a cache
that is empty after every restart because it lives in memory. The service now
fetches the catalog itself the first time anything needs it; transcription,
cover art, karaoke and the assistant all go through one place.

items.subject: fix(ui): name the model each role loads, ask for the quality the model can give
items.body: Two things the panel got wrong about what is actually happening.

items.subject: feat(assistant): carry MiniMax's caption skill whole, and route through it
items.body:
The assistant was following a transcription of MiniMax's demo prompt. They
publish the real thing with the model - the music-caption-rewriter skill: a
genre router, eighteen family indexes and a thousand complete captions written
the way Music3 wants to be addressed.

items.subject: feat(karaoke): time every word, not just the line
items.body:
A line time alone leaves a karaoke player one option - sweep the highlight
from the start of the line to the start of the next - and that drifts off the
singing within a couple of words. This is the whole point of karaoke timings,
so they are now per word.

items.subject: feat(ui): a first run that shows what it is about to do
items.body:
The old screen offered a radio list of profiles and hid the actual components
behind "show all profiles and manual assembly", so what would be downloaded,
and what was already here, took clicking to find out.

items.subject: docs: record karaoke and how the three recognisers actually performed
feat(ui): karaoke lives in the track menu, where the other track actions are
fix(openrouter): the recognisers were never in the catalog we fetched
items.body:
OpenRouter publishes speech-to-text models only behind
`?output_modalities=transcription`, and they declare their output as
"transcription" rather than "text". The catalog fetched the plain listing and
inferred capabilities from "text", so it knew of 38 audio-capable chat models
and not one dedicated recogniser - no Whisper, no Deepgram, no Chirp - and
karaoke on OpenRouter could only refuse.

items.subject: fix: find the models where they actually are, and say what a preset will cost
items.body: Two things a stray click exposed.

items.subject: feat(karaoke): the switch, the engine choice and the button on a track
items.body:
Settings gains a karaoke section: one switch, three recognisers, and only the
downloads the chosen one needs - Parakeet with its ONNX Runtime, Whisper with
its CUDA or CPU build and a model, OpenRouter with a model id. Off by default,
and with it off nothing about karaoke appears anywhere.

items.subject: feat(karaoke): time a track's own lyrics with a recogniser of the user's choice
items.body:
Karaoke needs timings, and the video studio has been able to draw them all
along - it parses LRC and renders the current line - but nothing produced the
file. This adds the half that was missing.

items.subject: chore: refresh the desktop lockfile after the zip dependency
docs: note where a locally built desktop binary expects the engine
fix(ui): say the service is down instead of demanding a 12 GB download
items.body:
When the local service stopped answering, every screen fell back to "no model
profile installed" and told the user to download the five Music3 components -
which are already on disk. The status polling now separates "nobody answered"
from "the service says it is not ready": the sidebar shows one honest line and
the create panel says the service is not running and needs a restart, with the
library left untouched.

items.subject: fix(ui): show the description, not the scaffolding, under a track title
items.body:
A caption for this model is a labelled document, so the library, search and
song lists were reading "Global Metadata Basic Attributes: bpm is 118. key is
F# minor..." as a subtitle. They now skip the section headings and the
technical attributes and start where the music is actually described.

items.subject: docs: record the final verification run
fix: keep the full request in a track's provenance, and give it a real title
items.body: Two things the rebuilt form exposed, both verified against real renders.

items.subject: feat(assistant): run a GGUF that is already on this machine, and explain failures
items.body:
Downloading a second copy of Gemma is pointless when the machine already keeps
one for another tool, so the managed mode now also accepts a path to any text
GGUF. It is used where it lies - nothing is copied - and the file is checked
for the GGUF magic before llama-server is asked to load it.

items.subject: docs: bring the handoff up to date with the rebuilt form and the assistant
feat: let Studio download and run the assistant model itself
items.body:
The assistant could only use OpenRouter or a server the user had already set
up. This adds the third way the request asked for: pick a model, press
Download, and Studio fetches it along with the llama.cpp runtime and runs
llama-server as a sidecar on demand.

items.subject: feat(ui): configure the optional writing assistant from Settings
items.body:
It could only be turned on by hand with a PUT to /v1/assistant/status, which
is not a feature anyone can use. Settings now carries the same three states
the service already supported - off, a local OpenAI-compatible server, or
OpenRouter - with the OpenRouter model picked from the live catalog filtered
to models that actually declare the text capability.

items.subject: refactor(ui): lay the request form out in cards, not a stack of accordions
items.body:
The fields were right but the arrangement was not: six collapsible sections
of equal weight, four identical grey toolbar buttons, and fixed-height boxes
for sections that routinely run past a thousand characters.

items.subject: feat: rebuild the request form the way this model is actually used
items.body:
The previous form was invented rather than researched. This one follows what
every implementation of MiniMax Music 3 agrees on - the reference client that
ships with the engine, ComfyUI's native nodes, MiniMax's model card and their
own demo Space:

items.subject: docs: record the restored Video Studio and its local encoding
feat: bring back ACE's Video Studio, encoding locally instead of on a server
items.body:
The video generator was dropped during the port because it rendered through
the ACE Node service. The composer itself is model-independent — canvas,
audio analyser, ten visualiser presets, particles, effects, text layers,
random picsum backgrounds, Pexels search, album art placement — so it is
restored exactly as it was, and only the parts that needed that service are
replaced:

fix(app): finish localisation and make the packaged app reach its own service
items.body: Two defects that only showed up in the real application:

items.subject: feat: expose the engine's per-request component choice and a real re-render dialog
items.body: Two things minimaxmusic.cpp can do that the studio could not reach:

items.subject: test: cover engine option persistence and the batch ceiling
feat: expose the engine's real launch options and honour --max-batch
items.body:
minimaxmusic.cpp takes launch flags that change how the whole session uses
the GPU, and none of them were reachable. Settings now has a Local engine
section for the real flags — keep models in VRAM (--keep-loaded), songs per
request (--max-batch), LM KV cache (--max-seq), and the diagnostics switches
(--no-fa, --no-batch-cfg, --clamp-fp16) — persisted with the studio settings.

items.subject: feat(library): make the import tab a working audio import
items.body:
The library carried an "Uploads" tab left over from ACE reference tracks; it
listed a collection this build no longer has and could only ever be empty.
Meanwhile POST /v1/library/import existed on the service with nothing in the
UI able to reach it.

items.subject: feat: measure track length from the audio and document the fork honestly
items.body:
Track length came from the engine's replay request, which is sparse: a
60-second track omits the duration field because 60 is the default, so the
library showed 0:00. Length is now measured from the rendered file — the WAV
header, or the declared bitrate for MP3 — which also gives imported audio a
real duration. A replay keeps the title of the track it reproduces instead of
deriving a new one from the caption.

items.subject: feat: ship the studio as one executable with its own icon
items.body:
The release was a launcher plus a second binary: the shell started
music-server.exe as a child process and had to find, wait for and later kill
it. The service is a Rust crate, so it is now a library the desktop binary
hosts on its own runtime thread. A release is a single .exe — no companion
program, no batch file, nothing left running if the window closes — and the
service in turn is the single owner of the minimaxmusic.cpp engine, which
removes the second, competing owner in the shell.

items.subject: fix(app): ship a real Tailwind build and repair the dark theme
items.body:
The studio pulled Tailwind from a CDN at every launch and declared its dark
surfaces as `dark:bg-suno-DEFAULT`. That class does not exist — Tailwind
exposes a palette's DEFAULT entry as `bg-suno` — so the setup screen, the
create panel and the library rendered on a white background while the rest
of the app was dark, and the whole layout collapsed to unstyled HTML
whenever the CDN was unreachable.

items.subject: fix(desktop,setup): make the shell actually launch and downloads actually resume
items.body:
Running the built desktop executable exposed three defects that a build
alone could not:

items.subject: fix(app): replace ACE-era row chrome with real Music3 provenance
items.body:
The library rows still described an ACE world: an "XL" model badge, an
"Unknown" creator with a link to a profile page that no longer exists, a
private/public lock for a single-user local library, and a workspace
breadcrumb for a workspace concept this build does not have.

items.subject: feat(app): move every studio screen onto the native Music3 API
items.body:
The UI no longer contains a client for the retired ACE Node service. What
changed, screen by screen:

items.subject: feat(server): restore the resource monitor as measured native telemetry
items.body:
ACE Studio had a resource readout and the first port dropped it. This
brings it back reading real values instead of estimates: GPU utilisation,
VRAM, temperature and power draw from nvidia-smi, system CPU and RAM, the
memory of the mm-server engine process and of the studio server itself.
Counters a card does not report stay absent instead of being shown as zero,
and the CPU sampler is primed so the first reading is not a fake 100%.

items.subject: chore: remove the inherited ACE-Step Studio sources
items.body:
This repository is a fork that replaces ACE inference with a native
MiniMax Music3 stack; the ACE sources live in their own repository and
carrying them here only produced screens and routes with no backend.

items.subject: fix(server): make model recommendation hardware-aware and drop phantom engines
items.body:
- /setup/status and the catalog now report the profile the machine can
  actually run (Full Native at >=20 GB, Q8 Quality at >=10 GB, Light only
  in the low-VRAM tier) instead of a fixed catalog constant, and readiness
  and remaining bytes are measured against the set the user selected.
- the unreachable native-balanced recommendation branch is removed and the
  GPU probe is cached, so setup polling no longer runs nvidia-smi per second.
- default and persisted configurations no longer name local engines this
  build does not ship (parakeet-tdt, local-llm); such selections are
  sanitized at startup.
- OpenRouter credentials can now be stored locally instead of requiring an
  environment variable, and are never serialized into any response.
- new GET /v1/engine/logs exposes the native mm-server log ring.
- generated songs get a readable title (explicit or derived) rather than
  storing the whole caption as the track name.
